title: 2 Chronicles 32
paragraphs: ¹ After all this, and after Hezekiah had firmly established his reforms, Sennacherib king of Assyria invaded Judah and besieged the fortified cities, planning to conquer them for himself. ² When Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come and that he intended to make war against Jerusalem, ³ he met with his officers and military commanders to plan how to cut off the water supply outside the city, and they gave him their full support. ⁴ A large force was gathered together and blocked all the springs and the streams flowing through the region. "Why should the kings of Assyria come here and find plenty of water?" they said. ⁵ Hezekiah also set about fortifying himself: he rebuilt the entire wall that had been broken down, raised towers on it, added a second outer wall, strengthened the Millo in the City of David, and produced large quantities of weapons and shields.

⁶ He appointed military commanders over the people, assembled them in the open square at the city gate, and spoke to encourage them: ⁷ "Be strong and courageous — do not be afraid or discouraged because of the king of Assyria and all his vast army. There is a greater power with us than with him. ⁸ He has only a human army, but we have the LORD our God to help us and to fight our battles." And the people were reassured by the words of Hezekiah king of Judah. ⁹ After this, while Sennacherib king of Assyria was attacking Lachish with all his forces, he sent his envoys to Jerusalem, to Hezekiah king of Judah and to all the people of Judah there, with this message: ¹⁰ "This is what Sennacherib king of Assyria says: What are you relying on to remain in Jerusalem under siege?"

¹¹ "Is Hezekiah not deceiving you, leading you to die by famine and thirst, when he tells you, 'The LORD our God will save us from the hand of the king of Assyria'? ¹² Is this not the same Hezekiah who removed the god's high places and altars, and ordered Judah and Jerusalem to worship only at one altar and burn incense on it? ¹³ Don't you know what I and my predecessors have done to all the peoples of other lands? Were the gods of those nations ever able to rescue their lands from my power? ¹⁴ Which of all the gods of those nations that my predecessors destroyed was able to save his people from my hand? How then can your god save you from my hand? ¹⁵ Don't let Hezekiah mislead you or deceive you like this. Don't believe him — no god of any nation or kingdom has ever been able to rescue his people from my hand or the hand of my predecessors. How much less will your god rescue you from my hand!"

¹⁶ His officers said still more against the LORD God and against his servant Hezekiah. ¹⁷ Sennacherib also wrote letters mocking the LORD, the God of Israel, saying, "Just as the gods of other nations did not save their people from my power, so the God of Hezekiah will not save his people from my hand." ¹⁸ Then they shouted out in Hebrew to the people of Jerusalem who were standing on the wall, trying to terrify and demoralize them so they could take the city. ¹⁹ They spoke about the God of Jerusalem the same way they spoke about the gods of the other peoples of the earth — as though he were merely the work of human hands. ²⁰ But Hezekiah the king and the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz cried out in prayer to heaven.

²¹ Then the LORD sent an angel who cut down every fighting man, leader, and officer in the camp of the Assyrian king. Sennacherib withdrew in disgrace to his own land. When he entered the temple of his god, his own sons struck him down with the sword there. ²² So the LORD saved Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib king of Assyria — and from every other threat as well — and gave them rest on all sides. ²³ Many came to Jerusalem to bring gifts to the LORD and valuable presents to Hezekiah king of Judah, and from that time on Hezekiah was held in high honor by all the nations. ²⁴ In those days Hezekiah became ill and was near death. He prayed to the LORD, who answered him and gave him a miraculous sign. ²⁵ But Hezekiah's heart became proud, and he did not respond in keeping with the mercy shown to him; so the LORD's wrath came upon him, and upon Judah and Jerusalem.

²⁶ Then Hezekiah humbled himself for his pride — he and the people of Jerusalem — so the LORD's wrath did not fall on them during the days of Hezekiah. ²⁷ Hezekiah became enormously wealthy and famous. He built treasuries to hold his silver, gold, precious stones, spices, shields, and all kinds of valuable objects. ²⁸ He made storehouses for the harvests of grain, wine, and oil, and stalls for all kinds of livestock, and pens for the flocks. ²⁹ He also built cities for himself and acquired great herds and flocks, for God had given him exceptional wealth. ³⁰ It was this same Hezekiah who blocked the upper outlet of the Gihon Spring and channeled the water straight down to the west side of the City of David. And Hezekiah succeeded in all that he undertook.

³¹ But when ambassadors arrived from the rulers of Babylon to ask about the miraculous sign that had occurred in the land, God withdrew from Hezekiah to test him — to find out what was truly in his heart. ³² The rest of the acts of Hezekiah and his faithful deeds are recorded in the vision of the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz, and in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel. ³³ Hezekiah died and was buried in the upper section of the tombs of the sons of David, and all of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem paid him great honor at his death. And his son Manasseh reigned in his place.
